assessment.rationale: This is the number the abstract did not give and the reason reading the full text mattered: the hypothesis previously had a direction and no magnitude, so it could not be checked against our noise floor. Two cautions. The measurement is terminal loss in nats at 0.12B under a large token budget, and ours is val_bpb at 50.33M under 300 seconds -- not the same quantity and not the same regime. And the retuned figure (0.015) is the honest one to carry, since the 0.028 partly measures a mistuned baseline rather than a missing component.

metrics.name: terminal_loss_delta
metrics.result: 0.015-0.028 nats at 0.12B. Retuning recovers roughly half, so about half the effect is a learning-rate interaction rather than the scale vector itself. Our gate is 0.000426 bpb and control sigma 0.004430, so even a fifth of this effect would be legible here.

locators.excerpt: Removing scale vectors reduces terminal loss by ~0.028 under same learning rate; even after retuning, models without scale vectors remain ~0.015 worse.
locators.location: full text, Figure 1 (scale vector ablation, 0.12B Llama)

scope.budget: industrial-scale token budgets; no wall-clock constraint
scope.model: dense and MoE decoder LLMs, 0.12B-2B, Pre-Norm with RMSNorm scale vectors

statement: On a 0.12B Llama-style Pre-Norm model, removing scale vectors raises terminal loss by about 0.028 nats at matched learning rate, and by about 0.015 nats even after the no-scale-vector model is retuned.
